A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, qualitative examples, and a 30-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds measured runtime and GPU-memory results in Appendix A.10.

M1.justification: Foreground extraction, summarization, recursive instruction generation, latent masking, ARO, and interactive editing retain the same procedures. Added descriptions of LLM interchangeability and component execution do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven academic-document topics, seven slide-deck topics, three-page instances, and seven background styles. v2 explains the synthetic benchmark's scope and exclusions more fully without adding evaluated domains or scenarios.

E2.justification: BAGEL and GPT-5 remain the evaluated external comparators, including in the new efficiency table. SD-Inpainting, Nano Banana 2, and additional layout-generation methods are discussed as exclusions rather than added to a documented comparative experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix A.10 introduces efficiency evaluation using three-page generation, peak GPU memory, and wall-clock time, specifying an A100 40GB for local configurations and client-side latency for GPT-5. Existing quality-evaluation settings remain unchanged. Fixed user-study ordering is newly disclosed, not identified as a changed procedure.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a component-cost analysis comparing LM alone, LM+ARO, and LM+ARO+MPC to isolate computational overhead. The existing readability and consistency ablations in Table 1 and Figure 6 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The user-study reporting is unchanged, and the new efficiency results provide single values without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All 63 numerical entries in Table 1 and the Figure 7 user-study results are unchanged. New Table 3 reports 246.00 seconds for BAGEL and LM alone, 247.26 for LM+ARO, 254.56 for the full system, and 324.00 for API-based GPT-5; local configurations report 31.3461 GB peak GPU memory.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(17), including the memory-window definition, masking updates, and contrast optimization, are retained. The new constant-memory remark explains the existing fixed-window design without adding a formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: foreground-preserving latent masking, automated contrast optimization, and recursive multi-page consistency within an editable layered framework.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the interpretation and applicability discussion. Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendices A.2–A.3 add extraction and transparent-overlay failure conditions, long-document validation limits, arguments about LLM independence and inpainting, and commercial applications. The claimed saturation beyond roughly ten pages and inpainting upper-bound argument are additional assertions without corresponding new validation.

D1.justification: v2 adds hardware and timing-measurement details, explains component execution costs, and identifies the participant pool as researchers, designers, and graduate students. Appendix A.9 newly discloses fixed output ordering and consistent evaluation instructions. Existing implementation hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to BizGen, Hybrid Layout Control for Diffusion Transformer, and CreatiDesign, with expanded discussion distinguishing fixed-document editing from layout generation. The WCAG reference is updated to 2.2. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 and the user-study description receive localized rewrites. Limitations move from the conclusion to Appendix A.2, and separate application and efficiency sections are added. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column layout with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. Figures 9 and 11 rearrange their comparison panels, Table 1 becomes substantially smaller, and Table 3 is added. The existing 39 figures are retained rather than replaced by new qualitative evidence.

improvement.justification: The efficiency measurements, explicit user-study ordering, and more specific applicability limits improve transparency and practical assessment. These are limited gains: the principal efficacy evidence is unchanged, some new inpainting and long-document assertions lack validation, and the smaller Table 1 reduces readability. Overall, the added reporting provides a modest quality improvement.
